statement: Every Cypher query has a SQL-path answer; a query the native executor does not support (or declines) is answered by the SQL path exactly as with the native executor off
Python builds the native plan and IRIS runs it; the native executor never parses Cypher text
ObjectScript class methods called over the Native API do not check SQL privileges (a caller without SQL SELECT can still read through them)
bulk_delete_adjacency is refused in strict mode and deletes nothing

delete_node / bulk_delete_nodes with graph omitted (not None) delete each ID from the one graph that holds it, a holder being a graph with a node row or an edge row naming the ID; with None they delete from the default graph.
A read scoped to one graph never returns content written to another graph.
In every native store, every graph-scoped entry has the graph key as its first subscript after the store's own node name.
Reading or clearing one graph touches only that graph's subtree: no other graph's entries are visited or changed.
SQL: the default graph is graph_id '' and a NULL graph_id also means the default graph for every SQL reader and writer.
A lookup with a key or graph name that has no content answers empty; it never falls back to the default graph or every graph.
Once any named graph holds an edge, every snapshot reader refuses or switches to the default graph's scoped index; none answers over all graphs merged.
A Cypher read without USE GRAPH answers the union (with multiplicity) of the answers each graph would give alone.
delete_node without detach (the default) is refused (node_has_relationships) while the default-graph node has live default-graph relationships
With auto-stubs, each stub op precedes its relationship and shifts positions; the returned reference names the shifted position
set/remove prop, add/remove label and delete_node on a non-node fail NodeNotFoundError
Ledger node operations read and write only default-graph node, label and property rows
In strict mode the listed calls (node and edge writes (create_node ... delete_node)) raise LedgerStrictModeError and change nothing
In strict mode the listed calls (erases (erase_graph/drop_graph, erase_all, delete_nodes_by_prefix)) raise LedgerStrictModeError and change nothing
In strict mode the listed calls (the store's write_nodes ... erase_bare_nodes) raise LedgerStrictModeError and change nothing
After a complete run no ledger record that belongs to the target (outside the listed exceptions) still holds its content.

Current behaviour: while strict mode stays on, a target whose graph still has node rows cannot be erased through the engine and its redaction is refused (target_live); the erase-then-redact sequence needs strict mode off.
Current behaviour: a record the run cannot attribute to the target (Matches answers unknown) stays in clear, and the receipt counts it in unattributed_records while still reporting complete.
A record outside the target graph never belongs to the target; with no prefix every record of the target graph belongs; with a prefix only records whose IDs begin with the match string do.

A relationship delete or detach delete inside a tenant's revision writes delete records for the relationship's reifier nodes with the reifier's own ID and the default graph; unless the reifier ID begins with the tenant's prefix, neither the tenant's graph target nor its prefix target tombstones them.
Start is refused (target_live) while any node, label, property or relationship row of the target is live.
A target_live refusal changes no record, marker, key or metadata.
The target_live refusal names the target and what is live.
The final step re-checks liveness under the head lock and refuses to finish (keeping the marker) if the target became live during the run.
Current behaviour: liveness counts rows only, so a target whose only live content is temporal-only edges is not refused and its temporal records are tombstoned while the events stay readable.
For a default-graph prefix target, a live node, label or property row of a matching ID in any graph refuses the redaction.

For the whole default graph (no prefix) a node row live in any graph must refuse the redaction; as built only default-graph rows are counted, so named-graph node records are tombstoned while the node is live.
For a default-graph target, relationship rows of other graphs do not refuse the redaction.
The four-field update is allowed only when the redaction's context names the row.
The redaction revision names each revision this run redacted, by seq, with its tombstone count.
After the erase alone (target records still in the ledger) verify reports a divergence.
When the ledger matched the store before the erase, nothing was written outside the ledger afterwards and the redacted targets cover everything erased, verify reports equal after erase and redaction.
Statement ID mismatches never produce differences
A second publishing rebuild of the interned snapshot (^NKG) while one runs waits or gets a documented busy result
Removing a triple from one graph keeps the interned snapshot's merged edge while another graph still holds the triple, and drops it when none does
With the index declared, every row insert, update or delete by any writer path (engine, store, Cypher, ledger, Eraser, raw SQL) changes the adjacency index accordingly
Without the declared index, the engine's own edge writers keep the adjacency index current
With no caller transaction open, bulk_load_session leaves ^NKG current when it returns
Inside a caller transaction bulk_load_session leaves ^NKG for sync() to rebuild
Every change to a node's outgoing adjacency moves its generation
A failed exclusive probe, the no-lock-writer flag or a generation change keeps the source from counting as filled
The interned snapshot (^NKG) records the token it was built from and is current only while that token is live
After an erasure the first algorithm reading the snapshot rebuilds it once, under a lock, before answering
An unmarked structural edge stays when its last timestamp goes
A Native Reader is used only for a default-graph call; a named-graph call is answered by its Owner
Owner and Native Reader answers are cached under the same key, which does not include the library build
Erasing a graph deletes that graph's rows from an orphan routed table and does not drop the table
After delete_node, the node stays findable through a named index until the caller deletes it from the index or rebuilds
Insert and Delete run under the index's write lock inside a transaction

The ^NKG-reading procedures (Cypher CALL ivg.betweenness/closeness/eigenvector/leiden/triangleCount/scc/kcore and the SQL kg_* functions) raise, naming the Python method to use, exactly when a graph other than the default holds an edge; otherwise they answer.
For the eight centrality/community algorithms the engine method and its CALL ivg.* procedure accept exactly the same option values and refuse the same ones with ValueError before reading data.
gamma is accepted in (0, 100] and refused otherwise.

A Cypher variable-length pattern returns one row per path (openCypher multiplicity) on the native and SQL paths: over a->x->b, a->y->b, a->b, *1..2 gives b three times and x, y once; *2..2 gives b twice; *0..1 includes a
The accelerator (Arno) BFS is chosen only for an outbound walk of the default graph while no other graph holds edges (and the library offers bfs)
Under USE GRAPH g every read clause of the query (MATCH, OPTIONAL MATCH, variable-length, procedure calls) reads only graph g, on the native and SQL paths
The native executor and the SQL path apply the same graph scope (USE GRAPH g, USE GRAPH '', none) to the same read
A failed Cypher write inside a caller transaction takes back only its own changes; the caller's earlier work stays pending
Values of one kind that are equal fall into one group / one DISTINCT value / one count(DISTINCT) unit, on the SQL path and the native executor
The native executor groups by typed value, so a grouped query over a number and its spelling answers different groups on the two paths
A query with OPTIONAL MATCH is never admitted to the native executor
An empty-string property sorts first as a string on the SQL path and with the nulls on the native executor
When either feed's MAX(ID) is below its watermark (reset, older restore) a sync runs a rebuild instead of applying feeds
A rebuild compares rather than erases, so surviving nodes keep their vectors
A graph erase resets the FHIR graph's interpretation version (NULL), marking it stale
After an erase the next sync re-derives and re-applies every resource from watermark 0 (the graph refills)
An ordinary erase keeps the graph's sync task, which keeps running
A graph erase removes compartment edges as ordinary edges

purge_before and set_temporal_structural run on the engine's own Native API connection when the engine knows its credentials (from_connect) and are durable whatever the caller does; on the caller's connection they follow the caller.
erase_graph/erase_all go through the engine's native connection: they join the caller's transaction on the caller's connection and commit on their own with from_connect.
erase_graph/erase_all go through the engine's native connection: they join the caller's transaction on the caller's connection and commit on their own with from_connect.
sync() and the temporal rebuilds run on the engine's native connection with the same join-or-own-transaction rule.
set_multigraph runs on the engine's native connection with the same join-or-own-transaction rule.
Named BM25 and vector index writes run on the engine's native connection with the same join-or-own-transaction rule.
FHIR graph calls run on the engine's native connection with the same join-or-own-transaction rule.
Node deletion removes the reifier nodes of the deleted node's edges in a later transaction, so the node delete can commit while the reifier cleanup fails.
delete_node removes the node, its labels and properties and every edge incident to it in its graph; other nodes stay.
delete_node also removes the node's documents and vectors (every routed vector table of the graph) in its graph.
After the node's delete, the reifier nodes of its edges are removed (in each graph holding them).
The node row and its own rows (labels, properties, documents, vectors, incident edges) are deleted in one transaction: all or none.
bulk_delete_nodes drops None and empty IDs, converts the rest to text and removes repeats before batching.
A node delete can finish before its reifier cleanup raises; the batch then counts as failed (false result) although the nodes are gone.
When the store's delete commits earlier chunks and a later chunk fails, the batch is counted failed and logged as rolled back although earlier chunks are deleted.
delete_edge removes every row of the triple from the given graph.
delete_edge(all_graphs=True) removes the triple from every graph.
delete_edge returns True when no row matched.
As built, delete_edge removes only the edge rows (and their adjacency), leaving the edge's reifications and edge embeddings.
delete_reification removes the reifier's link, properties, labels and node rows in every graph and keeps the edge.
^NKG holds one entry per triple whatever its multiplicity.
A degree answer equals the count of the node's adjacency entries at the time asked; no maintained counter answers it.
vec_search returns at most k stored IDs ordered nearest first
An insert at occupied coordinates changes nothing anywhere (raw, attributes, statistics, event counter, newest-event index, rows), so the statistics never count the second write.
The newest-event index stays exact through node erasure.
The newest-event index stays exact through graph erasure.
A backfill writes a marked structural edge and both nodes for every triple of the predicate that has a timestamp and no edge.
Erasing a node in g removes every temporal edge of g with that node as source or target, and none in other graphs.
After a committed node erasure the remaining statistics equal the surviving edges.
A login without %Native_GlobalAccess gets a warning and its engine is not checked (a mismatched engine is admitted)
On any IVG Schema, write, erase and read paths are at most 5% slower than baseline a42db224
Upgrade leaves legacy objects in place and working (except the Arno revoke)
Upgrade discards compiled Cypher plans built against the old names; none is reused
Upgrade revokes EXECUTE on the 4.5.x Arno SQL functions from every user and role except %All holders (warning when held through a schema-wide grant)
The Arno functions remain after the revoke
A replacing restore empties every graph and then loads the archive.
An archive with another layout is refused before erase; an unstamped archive is accepted.
snapshot_info version is the archive format '1.1'; the writing release is metadata.ivg_version.
snapshot_info of a ZIP without metadata.json raises KeyError.
ready_for_multihop_bfs does not require the integer adjacency copy
Variable-length Cypher matches answer without the integer adjacency copy
The sync state does not report whether the integer copy is built; adjacency.nkg_populated does
A delete or erase drops the integer copy and clears the flag; meanwhile the report says in sync and nkg_populated is False
After a delete or erase, the next reader of the integer copy rebuilds it
After the first sync(), each edge write interns its new triple in the integer copy
After a delete or erase, verify_sync reports drift until the integer copy is rebuilt, while the status report says in sync
engine.capabilities says what the namespace has deployed (classes, ^KG, ^NKG)
The store's capabilities() is a fixed catalogue of what the adapter implements (every algorithm True, only Arno entries live), not a report of what the namespace can run
With a declared adjacency index, the index always equals the canonical form of the rows, on every write path
sync() then rebuilds the interned snapshot (^NKG) from the adjacency index
After bulk loads and erasures the interned snapshot needs a rebuild
Without the Arno library, sync() still rebuilds the interned snapshot with the ObjectScript builder
